title: Preserve the stronger ordinary use of the same acquired representation
statement: A conventional positive-rate outer phase-error code corrects weak residual rotations rather than demanding all coherences remain almost fixed. Final trimming of CERTIFIED scalar coefficient bounds gives per-block O(n^-k) and the qualified horizon Omega(n^(2k)/log(1/delta)) at systematic coefficient precision O(n^-k). Protected syndrome ancillas, polynomial Clifford circuits, classical decoding, measurement and receiver noise are included in the stated protocol. O(n^2) classical wait has vanishing deep-noise contribution for k>=3; k=2 requires its finite constant budget. One final recovery pays preparation/records, with no storage-interval entropy outlet. Conventional coding also tolerates poorer calibration than the direct passive certificate; charging it passive precision would hide a real conventional advantage. This is a derived protocol, not a large quantum execution or independent audit.

requires: Actual Hermitian commuting collective fields L_a=sum_i w_ai Z_i, fixed rank r, acquired coefficient intervals and specified generator D[L_a]; this is not arbitrary local noise.
Fixed depth k complementary-pair hierarchy and actual encoders/receivers; suitable trajectory-containing invariant subspaces are required for the control theorem.
All pulse duration/precision, external faults, calibration, source, measurement, decoding and terminal noise costs remain charged.
